evals.name: checks-without-touching-settings
evals.expected_output: Reports jq presence, the installed shim state, the statusline wiring state, tee-file freshness against the 10-minute staleness rule, and the hook kill switch; prints the exact settings.json statusline edit for the operator; edits nothing.
expectations: Reads settings.json only; never writes settings, pluginConfigs, or the contract directory
Reports PASS/FAIL/INFO with one remediation line per FAIL
Prints the settings.json edit naming the shim's fixed ~/.claude/rate-limit-guard/bin/ path, never a version-pinned plugin-cache path
Surfaces the dotfiles-tracking reminder for the operator-owned edit

evals.name: distinguishes-unconfigured-from-wrapper-missing
evals.prompt:
/rate-limit-guard:setup check

My settings.json has no statusLine key at all.
evals.expected_output: States that no statusline is configured (as opposed to a wrapper missing from an existing command) and prints the standalone wiring variant, not the wrapping variant.
expectations: Names the state as no-statusline-configured, not as a broken wrapper
Prints the standalone shim command with no wrapped command
Does not offer to apply the settings edit itself

evals.name: reads-absent-rate-limits-as-reactive-only
evals.prompt:
/rate-limit-guard:setup check

The tee file is fresh but has no rate_limits key.
evals.expected_output: Reports the fresh-but-windowless snapshot as INFO — this auth exposes no subscription windows, consumers correctly run reactive-only — not as a failure to fix.
expectations: Classifies absent rate_limits on a fresh snapshot as expected fail-open behavior
Does not tell the operator to rewire or reinstall anything for it
Cites the reader contract as the owner of the fail-open rule

evals.name: flags-legacy-version-pinned-wiring
evals.prompt:
/rate-limit-guard:setup check

My settings.json statusLine command is: bash "~/.claude/plugins/cache/melodic-software/rate-limit-guard/0.1.0/scripts/statusline-tee.sh" ~/.claude/statusline/render.sh — and that file exists right now.
evals.expected_output: Names the wiring as legacy version-pinned even though the file exists today: it stops teeing at the next version bump and breaks the whole statusline once the old version directory is pruned. Prints the shim wiring as the fix, with apply first if the shim is not installed.
expectations: Does not treat current file existence as evidence the wiring is healthy
Names both failure modes: silent tee stop on version bump, and statusline breakage after the ~14-day prune
Prints the shim-based replacement wiring and sequences apply before the settings edit when the shim is absent

evals.name: apply-installs-shim-byte-identically-and-idempotently
evals.expected_output: Copies the shipped statusline-shim.sh byte-identically to ~/.claude/rate-limit-guard/bin/statusline-shim.sh, reports the write (or reports no change on a second identical run), states that the shim is inert until the operator wires it, and prints the wiring edit as the next step.
expectations: Writes only ~/.claude/rate-limit-guard/bin/statusline-shim.sh — never settings.json, rate-limits.json, stop-events.jsonl, or the sibling context-guard directory
Installed copy is byte-identical to the shipped source, not a rewritten or templated variant
Second identical apply reports no content change
States that installing the shim starts nothing until the settings.json wiring is applied by the operator

evals.name: composes-without-double-wrapping
evals.prompt:
/rate-limit-guard:setup check

My statusLine command is already: bash ~/.claude/context-guard/bin/statusline-shim.sh ~/.claude/statusline/render.sh — I configured context-guard first. Both plugins are installed, but I have never run /rate-limit-guard:setup apply.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the existing sibling-shim wrapper, unwraps it to the operator's own renderer before composing, and prints wiring that runs each tee exactly once. Because this plugin's own shim is not installed yet, it reports that and names apply as the remediation rather than printing wiring naming a file that does not exist.
expectations: Treats ~/.claude/statusline/render.sh as the wrapped command — never re-wraps the full existing command, so the context-guard shim appears exactly once in the printed wiring
Never prints a combined form naming a shim path that is not installed; gates the combined wiring on the sibling shim existing, or directs the operator to run that plugin's apply first
Explains that a duplicated tee runs and writes on every refresh and adds another ~0.6-0.9 s per refresh
Still edits nothing — the wiring is printed for the operator to apply

evals.name: uninstall-order-unwrap-before-delete
evals.prompt:
/rate-limit-guard:setup check

How do I back this out completely? I want to remove the plugin and everything it put on my machine.
evals.expected_output: Gives the two operator cleanup steps in a REQUIRED order: unwrap the statusLine command first, then delete ~/.claude/rate-limit-guard/.
expectations: States the order explicitly and gives the reason: deleting the directory first leaves settings.json invoking a missing file, so bash exits 127 and the whole statusline goes down
Does not present the two steps as order-independent
Notes that uninstalling the plugin itself is safe on its own — the shim degrades to running the wrapped command
